question.text: A mass of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>10</mn><mi mathvariant="normal"> </mi><mi>kg</mi></math> is suspended vertically by a rope from the roof. When a horizontal force is applied on the rope at some point, the rope deviated at an angle of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>45</mn><mo>°</mo></math> at the roof point. If the suspended mass is at equilibrium, the magnitude of the force applied is <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mfenced separators="|"><mrow><mi>g</mi><mo>=</mo><mn>10</mn><mi> </mi><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></mfenced></math>

solution.text:
Tcos⁡45°=mg

Tsin⁡45°=F

tan 45°=Fmg

F=mg=100 N
